descriptions.tagline: A desktop weather radar that reads the raw data itself.
descriptions.short: Free, open source weather radar for Windows. It decodes NEXRAD Level II volumes, MRMS national grids, GOES lightning and GFS wind on your own machine and draws them on a GPU vector map. No account, no API key, no ads.
descriptions.long:
OpenRadar is a map-first desktop weather radar for Windows. Rather than showing pictures a service already drew, it decodes the raw products in Rust on your own machine: NEXRAD Level II volumes with velocity dealiasing and cross-sections, MRMS national grids, GOES lightning, GFS wind, HRRR smoke and forecast reflectivity. Warnings, storm reports, river gauges, soundings and satellite sit over the same map, and every reading carries the source it came from and how old it is.

It is one window. Pan the planet, zoom from a globe down to a street, and scrub two hours of radar without the map moving under you. Nothing is uploaded, there is no account, and an offline cache means a launch with no network still opens on the last picture you saw.

MIT licensed. English, Spanish and Canadian French.
